draft.title: Symbolism in literature
card: A symbol is an object, character, colour or setting that stands for an idea. A dove can stand for peace, and a red rose can stand for love.
A symbol is still a real thing in the story. A dove is a bird on the page, and it also points to an idea beyond itself.
A symbol can gather meaning across a text. If a writer keeps returning to the same object, each appearance can add to what it stands for.
To read a symbol, ask what the thing is, where it appears, and what idea it seems to point to. Look for clues in the text that support your reading.
draft.remember: A symbol is a thing that stands for an idea, and its meaning can grow each time it returns.

a.q: Ravi longs to leave his small town for the city. In the opening, middle and closing scenes, he stops at the same locked gate at the town's edge. What idea does the gate most likely stand for?
opts: Being held back from the life he wants
The freedom to choose his own path
His pride in the town he grew up in
His joy at starting a new journey
a.why: Ravi wants a life beyond the town, and the gate between him and the road out is locked each time he stands there. So it points to being held back. Freedom is the opposite, because a locked gate stops him from going where he wants.
a.clue: Think about what Ravi wants and what a locked gate does.

b.q: In a novel, Lena's grandmother's old teapot is on the table during a family fight, a house move and a reunion. It is always kept safe. What does the teapot most likely come to stand for?
opts: A family bond that lasts through every change
The arguments that keep dividing the family
The family's wish to throw out the past
The family's wealth and costly belongings
b.why: The teapot returns at each major family event, including the reunion, and is always kept safe, so it gathers the meaning of a bond that survives change. The arguments are tempting, but they are only one of the scenes, and the teapot is protected through all of them.
b.clue: Look at every scene it appears in, not just one.

a.best: Being held back from the life he wants

b.best: A family bond that lasts through every change
